next_step: Run 2-week lat/throughput POC on Dedicated nodes; collect p95/p99 traces; finalize SSO SOW.
notes:
High-sensitivity fintech client building low-latency alerting and conversational analyst assistant. Primary constraint: live signal processing pipeline requires end-to-end p95 latency <= 75ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens) under steady-state 400-600 req/s. Cost target: reduce per-1000-token cost relative to current managed endpoint by ~40% without losing >=95% of current answer quality. Interest in Redwood Optimize: batching recommendations, prefix/KV caching, and model quantization (8-bit/4-bit GPTQ-style) to hit cost goals. They're explicitly asking for detailed perf benchmarking: p50/p95/p99, memory/KV cache hit rates, token throughput per GPU, and token-cost tradeoff curves across model variants.

POC ask: 2-week Dedicated POC (reserved small pool) with scripted load generator (we'll provide scripts). Evaluate (A) baseline FP16 model, (B) 8-bit quantized, (C) 4-bit GPTQ run, with and without prefix caching, with autoscale policy simulation. They want breakdowns by routing policy — region fallback and cheaper-model fallback — and a test to verify graceful degradation under node failures.

Security: must pass SOC2 checklist + customer-managed KMS for key rotation. Data residency: primary data must remain in us-east-1. Legal flagged retention/PII clauses; wants retention_controls features in Redwood Console.

Quoted from CTO call: "We need deterministic tail latency — if it spikes, trading signals lose value. Also show us a clear cost model: if we quantize to 8-bit, what do we really give up, and where is the sweet spot?"

AE notes: good product fit for Dedicated + Optimize. High probability to expand to Private if SSO/KMS roadmap aligns. Procurement timeline depends on legal sign-off; finance needs ARR band justification for reserved capacity. POC budget pre-approved up to $15k spend for performance validation.
